chapter: Piano influences and the New Orleans scene
title: Drummers and New Orleans musicians he knows
summary: He names Earl Palmer and other drummers, Roy Brown, Sugar Boy, Eddie Bo and Johnny Adams, and says he knows practically every musician in town.

bands.name: Sugar Boy and the Cane Cutters

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Earl Palmer, that was my favorite right drummer. Earl Palmer? He's in LA now. Oh, yeah. Big guy. George Palmer.
Yeah, George Parker, he was a good drummer, he's up there too.
Roy Brown, I met him up there. Yeah.

I met a bunch of studs from up there. I just can't call their names cause they wasn't popular, you know what I mean, but they could play but they never was on nothing. You know, there's fill-in men, call them out to sit in on sessions and things like that. Well, it ain't hauling nobody here, Sugar Boy, Eddie Bowe, I know practically any musician
here. Yeah, I used to see when I was, when I was 15, 14, 15, I used to see Sugar Boy and the Cane Cutters all the time, and Eddie Bowe, Oliver Morgan, and who else?

See Herman Thomas, Benny Spellman all the time. Yeah, she used to work on, I'm saying, I'm a little, I'm a little, I'm a little, Johnny Adams, he's got a pretty good thing going now. There's two good things I've heard, just Release Me.
Oh man, Release Me, that thing he's got going now is really good.
And that boy is terrific, you know what I mean, I'm not bragging on him with his thing.
Man, who's playing guitar on that record? With Johnny? Yeah.

I don't know, Johnny, he's a jumpy fella, you know. Truthfully, I mean, I don't think he did none of those numbers. He might have did Release Me here, this other number here, I mean, I don't even remember nobody saying that he was going to record anything. It just popped up, you know. Well, he did that, he must have just came from wherever he was, this way, you know. Usually a song will travel where you came from, all the time, you know. But there ain't nothing that I don't hardly know or have to work with or work for, or work for me or with me.
